newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Canada sign pact to develop satellites.
newsitem.headline: India, Canada sign pact to develop satellites.

text.p: India and Canada signed an agreement on Tuesday to develop satellites for space research and tap an international market for satellite data, officials said.

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) signed the agreement, described by ISRO's chairman, Krishnaswamy Kasturirangan, as a precursor for joint technology development missions.
Canadian officials said the two agencies would support each other in telemetry, tracking and control of spacecraft.
Among the commercial ventures being examined were value added products from data beamed by the Indian remote sensing satellites, Indian officials said.

PCI enterprises, an Ontario-based company, is likely to sign a deal with ISRO's commercial arm, Antrix Corporation, to market worldwide a software package called Spans (for special analysis) along with the remote sensing data of the Indian satellites, officials said.
